checks_run.procedure: Re-prove F-DG1-130. Plant the three assigned forms into a transformations module file via fileViolations('transformations', <MODULES_DIR>/transformations/zz-planted.ts, src): the named import, the namespace form, and the string key (crypto as any)["setEngine"]. Add 11 adversarial spellings (aliased import, destructured alias, default member, unicode-escaped identifier, escaped string key, template key, re-export, renamed re-export, optional chain, dynamic literal import, bare string literal) and 3 constructed keys.
checks_run.command: npx vitest run --project unit-node apps/api/src/zz-r10-probe.test.ts (clone only; source saved as zz-r10-probe.test.ts.txt)
checks_run.expected: each setEngine spelling is a 'native loader … setEngine' violation; constructed keys are rule-2 violations
checks_run.actual: A1/A2/A3 (assigned) and X1-X11 are all violations: 'native loader via setEngine', '.setEngine()', '["setEngine"]', 'a destructured setEngine', 'the "setEngine" key as a value'. Y1-Y3 are 'computed member with a non-literal key'. The probe test passed 24/24.

checks_run.procedure: Independently enumerate the own properties of node:{crypto, fs, fs/promises, os, path, url, util} and the namespaces fs.promises, path.posix/win32, util.types, crypto.webcrypto/subtle, crypto.constants and os.constants. Name-match them for loader/exec/native/debug terms and review each match and the full lists by hand. Check behaviourally that crypto.setFips does not dlopen a caller-supplied path, with setEngine as the control.
checks_run.command: node member-audit.mjs (saved as member-audit.mjs.txt); R10_MARKER=… node -e 'crypto.setFips(<eng.so>)'; control: crypto.setEngine(<eng.so>)
checks_run.environment: $TMPDIR scratch, node v22.22.2 / OpenSSL 3.5.5, gcc; OPENSSL_CONF/OPENSSL_MODULES unset
checks_run.expected: setEngine is the only native/loader/exec member, matching the header's audit
checks_run.actual: 503 members enumerated. Name matches: crypto getFips/setEngine/setFips; fs ftruncate/link/open*/opendir/readlink/symlink/truncate/unlink; os.loadavg; util callbackify/debug/debuglog/getCallSite(s)/inspect; util.types isModuleNamespaceObject/isNativeError; subtle.importKey; crypto.constants ENGINE_METHOD_* (numbers); os.constants.dlopen (RTLD_* numbers). Only setEngine loads code. setFips(<.so path>) ran no constructor (marker absent) and only toggles FIPS mode. setEngine(<.so>) ran the constructor (marker present). The audit agrees with the header (architecture.testkit.ts:46-57). No missed member.

Then run end to end with a real module file and a gcc-built constructor .so.
checks_run.command: same probe test (BYPASS block); R10_MARKER=… R10_SO=… npx vitest run --project unit-node apps/api/src/zz-r10-enum-e2e.test.ts with src/modules/transformations/zz-enum.ts planted (clone only)
checks_run.environment: disposable clone @241a377, node v22.22.2 / OpenSSL 3.5.5, gcc
checks_run.expected: every route to setEngine that is visible in module source is a violation, or the header names it as a residual
checks_run.actual: B1/B2/B3: n=0 (BYPASS-PASSES-LINT). End to end: moduleViolations('transformations') = [] with zz-enum.ts present. At runtime the .so ELF constructor ran (NATIVE-CONSTRUCTOR-RAN; marker file present) before setEngine threw ERR_CRYPTO_ENGINE_UNKNOWN. Raised as F-DG1-132 (Low, non-mandatory).

summary: PASS on candidate 18fee161. F-DG1-130 is verified: crypto.setEngine is a 'native loader' violation in all three assigned forms and in 11 further spellings. node:crypto with randomUUID/createHash stays allowed, architecture.test.ts passes 105/105, and the real tree has 0 violations. My independent member audit of the 7 allow-listed built-ins (503 members, Node 22.22.2) agrees with the header. New finding F-DG1-132 (Low, non-mandatory): enumerating the allowed namespace (new Map(Object.entries(c)).get("set"+"Engine" via join)) still reaches setEngine with 0 lint violations, and the native constructor runs end to end. The header's 'every form' claim is overstated. All required checks pass (integration 200/200 twice). Node 24 and AC-1 effect are BLOCKED on the environment. No Critical/High/mandatory finding is open.
